summary: Oswald Richter specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig (~1893–1897) under Karl Brugmann, and held posts at the Museum of Ethnology, Dresden (1898) and the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (1904).

Otakar Klíma studied Iranian, Central Asian studies, and linguistics at Charles University (Ph.D. 1927–1932) under Bedřich Hrozný, Vincenc Lesný, and Jan Rypka. From 1953 to 1973, he served as a departmental section director at the Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences.

Otakar Pertold was an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Charles University (Ph.D. ~1902–1908, habilitation ~1908–1912) and under mentors including Josef Zubatý, Wilhelm Geiger, and Paul Deussen, he held successive teaching posts at Charles University between 1912 and 1955.

An Indologist, Othmar Frank studied at the University of Paris (~1807–1811) and under Alexander Hamilton (1814). He served as professor at the University of Bamberg (~1803–1804), the University of Würzburg (1821), and the University of Munich (1826).
Indologist Otoya Tanaka studied at the University of Tokyo (~1924–1927) under Naoshiro Tsuji (~1924–1928). He later served as a professor at Chuo University (~1957–1974).

Otto Albert Paul worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Munich (Ph.D. 1924–1927) under Wilhelm Geiger, later directing the Institut zur Erforschung der Judenfrage in 1941.

Archaeologist Otto Benndorf studied at the universities of Bonn (~1856–1863) and Göttingen under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl and Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker. He held posts at Zurich, Munich, Charles University, and Vienna, and directed the Austrian Archaeological Institute (1898–1907).
Otto Blau studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1848) under August Friedrich Pott and at the University of Leipzig (~1850–1852).

Indologist and linguist Otto Donner studied at the University of Helsinki (Ph.D. ~1861–1863) and in Berlin and Tübingen under Albrecht Weber, Heymann Steinthal, and Rudolf von Roth. He served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative philology at Helsinki (1875–1905).

Historian of mathematics Otto E. Neugebauer completed his Ph.D. at Göttingen (~1924–1926) and studied under Boris Turayev. He held positions at Göttingen, the University of Copenhagen (1933–1939), Brown University (1939–1969), and the Institute for Advanced Study (1945; 1969–1990).

Otto Fischer worked in Sinology, Japanology, and art history, completing his habilitation at the University of Göttingen (~1908–1912). He directed the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart (1920) and Kunstmuseum Basel (1927), and was professor of art history at the University of Basel (~1927–1937).

Sinologist and Indologist Otto Franke studied at Göttingen (Ph.D. 1884–1886) under Franz Kielhorn, as well as under Carl Arendt and Wilhelm Grube. He held chairs at the Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut/University of Hamburg (1909–1923) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1923–1931).

Otto Fredrik Tullberg studied linguistics and Indology at Uppsala University (M.A. 1822–1830) and under scholars including Franz Bopp, Eugène Burnouf, and Horace Hayman Wilson. In 1843, he was appointed Professor of Oriental Languages at Uppsala University.
Otto Grohma, a scholar of Indology and archaeology, earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (~1964–1971) and became an assistant there in 1972.

Linguist and Iranian specialist Otto Heinrich Wilhelm Keller earned his Ph.D. at the University of Giessen (1897–1904) under Christian Bartholomae. He later served as director at Gymnasium Michelstadt (1918) and Wolfgang-Ernst-Gymnasium (1925–1935).

Linguist Otto Hoffmann completed his Ph.D. at Göttingen (1883–1888) under August Fick. He held academic posts at the University of Königsberg (1889–1896), the University of Breslau (1907–1909), and the University of Münster (1909–1935).

Religious studies scholar Otto Huth completed his Ph.D. at the University of Bonn (1925–1932) after studying theology at Kiel and Marburg. He served as a Privatdozent at Strasbourg (1941–1944) and as a professor at the University of Tübingen (1942–1971).

Otto Höfler was a scholar of linguistics and religion who earned his PhD (1920–1926) and habilitation (~1926–1931) at Vienna under Rudolf Much. He held professorships at Kiel (1935), Munich (1938–1945; 1954), and Vienna (1957–1971).

Archaeologist and linguist Otto Jahn studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Berlin between 1831 and 1836. He held posts at the universities of Kiel (~1839–1845), Greifswald (~1845–1847), Leipzig (~1847–1851), and Bonn (~1855–1869).

Otto K. Schwarz studied religious and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD at the Russian Christian Academy for the Humanities (2021–2025). He joined the Higher School of Economics as a faculty member in 2026.
